{{Short description|Generalization of a foliation}}
In mathematics, a '''Haefliger structure''' on a [[topological space]] is a generalization of a [[foliation]] of a [[manifold]], introduced by [[André Haefliger]] in 1970.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Haefliger |first=André |year=1970 |title=Feuilletages sur les variétés ouvertes |journal=[[Topology (journal)|Topology]] |volume=9 |issue=2 |pages=183–194 |doi=10.1016/0040-9383(70)90040-6 |issn=0040-9383 |mr=0263104 |doi-access= |authorlink=André Haefliger}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Haefliger |first=André |title=Manifolds--Amsterdam 1970 (Proc. Nuffic Summer School) |publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] |year=1971 |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics, Vol. 197 |volume=197 |location=Berlin, New York |pages=133–163 |chapter=Homotopy and integrability |doi=10.1007/BFb0068615 |isbn=978-3-540-05467-2 |mr=0285027 |authorlink=André Haefliger}}</ref> Any foliation on a manifold induces a special kind of Haefliger structure, which uniquely determines the foliation.

==Definition==
A codimension-''<math>q</math>'' '''Haefliger structure''' on a topological space ''<math>X</math>'' consists of the following data:

* a [[Cover (topology)|cover]] of ''<math>X</math>'' by [[Open set|open sets]] <math>U_\alpha</math>;
* a collection of [[continuous maps]] ''<math>f_\alpha: X \to \mathbb{R}^q</math>'';
* for every ''<math>x \in U_\alpha \cap U_\beta</math>'', a [[diffeomorphism]] ''<math>\psi_{\alpha \beta}^x</math>'' between [[Open neighbourhood|open neighbourhoods]] of ''<math>f_\alpha(x)</math>'' and ''<math>f_\beta(x)</math>'' with ''<math>\Psi^x_{\alpha \beta} \circ f_\alpha = f_\beta</math>'';

such that the continuous maps ''<math>\Psi_{\alpha \beta}: x \mapsto \mathrm{germ}_x (\psi^x_{\alpha \beta})</math>'' from <math>U_\alpha \cap U_\beta</math> to the [[Sheaf (mathematics)|sheaf]] of [[germ (mathematics)|germ]]s of local diffeomorphisms of <math>\R^q</math> satisfy the 1-cocycle condition
:<math>\displaystyle\Psi_{\gamma\alpha}(u) = \Psi_{\gamma\beta}(u)\Psi_{\beta\alpha}(u)</math> for <math>u\in U_\alpha\cap U_\beta\cap U_\gamma.</math>

The cocycle ''<math>\Psi_{\alpha \beta}</math>'' is also called a '''Haefliger cocycle'''.

More generally, ''<math>\mathcal{C}^r</math>'', [[Piecewise linear function|piecewise linear]], [[Analytic function|analytic]], and continuous Haefliger structures are defined by replacing sheaves of germs of smooth diffeomorphisms by the appropriate sheaves.

== Examples and constructions ==

=== Pullbacks ===
An advantage of Haefliger structures over foliations is that they are closed under [[Pullback (category theory)|pullbacks]]. More precisely, given a Haefliger structure on ''<math>X</math>'', defined by a Haefliger cocycle ''<math>\Psi_{\alpha \beta}</math>'', and a continuous map ''<math>f: Y \to X</math>'', the '''pullback Haefliger structure''' on ''<math>Y</math>'' is defined by the open cover <math>f^{-1}(U_\alpha)</math> and the cocycle ''<math>\Psi_{\alpha \beta} \circ f</math>''. As particular cases we obtain the following constructions:

* Given a Haefliger structure on ''<math>X</math>'' and a subspace ''<math>Y \subseteq X</math>'', the '''restriction of the Haefliger structure''' to ''<math>Y</math>'' is the pullback Haefliger structure with respect to the inclusion ''<math>Y \hookrightarrow X</math>''
* Given a Haefliger structure on ''<math>X</math>'' and another space ''<math>Y</math>'', the '''product of the Haefliger structure''' with ''<math>Y</math>'' is the pullback Haefliger structure with respect to the projection ''<math>X \times Y \to X</math>'' 

=== Foliations ===
Recall that a codimension-''<math>q</math>'' [[foliation]] on a smooth manifold can be specified by a covering of ''<math>X</math>'' by open sets <math>U_\alpha</math>, together with a [[submersion (mathematics)|submersion]] ''<math>\phi_\alpha</math>'' from each open set <math>U_\alpha</math> to <math>\R^q</math>, such that for each <math>\alpha, \beta</math> there is a map ''<math>\Phi_{\alpha \beta}</math>'' from <math>U_\alpha \cap U_\beta</math> to local diffeomorphisms with 
:<math>\phi_\alpha(v)= \Phi_{\alpha,\beta}(u)(\phi_\beta(v))</math>
whenever ''<math>v</math>'' is close enough to ''<math>u</math>''. The Haefliger cocycle is defined by
:<math>\Psi_{\alpha,\beta}(u) = </math> germ of <math>\Phi_{\alpha,\beta}(u)</math> at ''u''.

As anticipated, foliations are not closed in general under pullbacks but Haefliger structures are. Indeed, given a continuous map ''<math>f: X \to Y</math>'', one can take pullbacks of foliations on ''<math>Y</math>'' provided that ''<math>f</math>'' is [[Transversality (mathematics)#Transversality of maps|transverse]] to the foliation, but if ''<math>f</math>'' is not transverse the pullback can be a Haefliger structure that is not a foliation.

==Classifying space==
Two Haefliger structures on ''<math>X</math>'' are called '''concordant''' if they are the restrictions of Haefliger structures on ''<math>X \times [0,1]</math>'' to ''<math>X \times 0</math>'' and ''<math>X \times 1</math>''.

There is a classifying space <math>B\Gamma_q</math> for codimension-''<math>q</math>'' Haefliger structures which has a universal Haefliger structure on it in the following sense. For any topological space ''<math>X</math>'' and continuous map from ''<math>X</math>'' to <math>B\Gamma_q</math> the pullback of the universal Haefliger structure is a Haefliger structure on ''<math>X</math>''. For [[well-behaved]] topological spaces ''<math>X</math>'' this induces a 1:1 correspondence between homotopy classes of maps from ''<math>X</math>'' to <math>B\Gamma_q</math> and concordance classes of Haefliger structures.
